IncidentBot: PagerDuty SIREN — inference-gateway 5xx rate spike detected (>4% over 5m). Page fired to oncall rotation. Alert key: pd_inc_4543219876
PagerDuty: SEV2 — inference-gateway: 5xx-rate 4.8% (5m), approx 12k rps. auto-escalation enabled.
Maya (oncall): ack — I’m on it, checking dashboards and logs :eyes:
Maya (oncall): seeing concentrated spike from eu-west1 (hostpool-gw-*) and elevated upstream timeouts (upstream=runtime-kv-cache).
Ashwin: did we push anything to routing or gateway configs around 00:10–00:15?
Eli: @Ashwin yes — lightweight routing policy change (prefer batch-path v2) went at 00:12 as part of canary. Canary was ~15% of traffic.
Maya (oncall): copying logs — example 502s from gateway: ```
2026-03-15T00:13:02Z gateway-1 ERROR request_id=abc123 upstream_timeout=1201ms status=502 path=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T00:13:05Z gateway-2 ERROR request_id=abc124 upstream_error="kv cache miss + backend overload" status=502
```
Maya (oncall): metrics shell: `curl -s http://metrics.internal/alerts?m=inference.gateway.errors|rate` -> current: 4.8% (5m), spike started ~00:11.
ops-rotator: @Maya scheduled to swap canary back if needed. Ready to execute route rollback.
Maya (oncall): plan: 1) roll routing change back 2) scale dedicated worker pool +20% 3) add temporary gateway timeout bump to 5s to reduce upstream quick-fails. Going to run step 1 now.
Ashwin: log snippet from router confirms increased queue latencies at same time as canary ramp: ```
[00:12:10] router INFO route=batch-v2 latency_p50=35ms p95=420ms p99=1.2s
[00:12:11] router WARN queue_depth=180 target=80
```
Eli: KV cache eviction storms also show up in redis-latency graphs at 00:12 — probable cascading tail.
ops-rotator: rolling back route -> `infractl route set-weight batch-v2 0 --canary` (executed). :white_check_mark:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty note: rollback annotated by ops-rotator.
Maya (oncall): scaling workers: `k scale deployment/inference-workers --replicas=$(( $(k get deploy inference-workers -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}') * 1.2 ))` -> kicked a scale job.
Maya (oncall): temporarily increasing gateway timeout: `kubectl set env deploy/gateway TIMEOUT_MS=5000` (applied).
Ashwin: monitoring logs — immediate tail error slope reduced. p95 latencies improving.
Eli: after rollback and scale, KV misses dropped and redis latencies dipped back to normal range.
Maya (oncall): 00:28 snapshot: 5xx rate at 0.9% (5m), traffic returning to normal.
PagerDuty: Alert trend shows decline. No new pages in the last 5m.
Maya (oncall): confirming customer impact — there's a handful of failed requests for high-concurrency customers (internal ticket numbers attached), but no systemic data loss. Notified SRE-customer-facing.
Ashwin: next steps — open an incident runbook entry: root cause likely routing canary + cache eviction -> backpressure -> upstream timeouts. Recommend: add gradual canary ramping with circuit breakers + guardrail that aborts canary if queue_depth >100.
Eli: also add a short-term mitigator: throttle batch-path requests during cache-stress windows, and increase cache replication/priming for batch workloads.
Maya (oncall): creating incident doc and will request postmortem owners: @Ashwin (routing), @Eli (runtime cache), @ops-rotator (ops).
Maya (oncall): marking the PagerDuty alert as resolved (manual) and leaving a note for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
PagerDuty: Pager resolved by Maya at 00:33.
IncidentBot: Auto-note: please create a postmortem within 72 hours and include perf traces and the canary ramp timeline.
Maya (oncall): handing off to morning oncall @ops-rotator for follow-up and customer comms. Thanks team. :pray: 
ops-rotator: got it, will shepherd postmortem & stitch customer notes.
Maya (oncall): closing thread, will link incident doc here when ready.
